claim: Activation of the Norrin/Frizzled4 signalling axis inhibits medulloblastoma initiation in the Ptch+/− mouse model.
source: We show that activation of the vascular regulatory signalling axis mediated by Norrin (an atypical Wnt)/Frizzled4 (Fzd4) inhibits MB initiation in the Ptch+/− mouse model.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing reduced tumor incidence and increased latency when Norrin/Fzd4 signaling is intact.

claim: Loss of Norrin/Fzd4-mediated signalling in endothelial cells increases the frequency of pre-tumor lesions in Ptch+/− mice.
source: Loss of Norrin/Fzd4-mediated signalling in endothelial cells, either genetically or by short-term blockade, increases the frequency of pre-tumor lesions and creates a tumor-permissive microenvironment at the earliest, preneoplastic stages of MB.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by data in Figure 4 showing increased lesion numbers in compound mutants.

claim: The pro-tumor stroma induced by loss of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling is characterized by angiogenic remodelling.
source: This pro-tumor stroma, characterized by angiogenic remodelling, is associated with an accelerated transition from preneoplasia to malignancy.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this, supported by immunostaining data in Figures 5 and 6 showing vascular changes.

claim: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant brain tumor in children.
source: Medulloblastoma (MB), the most common malignant brain tumor in children, has become a paradigm for the study of pediatric tumors and primary brain tumors
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, representing general scientific knowledge.

claim: The Ptch+/− mouse is a model of human Gorlin syndrome predisposition to medulloblastoma.
source: An effective surrogate to test these interactions endogenously is the Ptch+/− mouse (Goodrich et al., 1997), a model of the human predisposition to MB (Gorlin syndrome) that, along with a subset of sporadic MB, belong to the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) subgroup (Taylor et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Goodrich et al., 1997; Taylor et al., 2012).

claim: Ptch+/− mice progress through well-defined stages of tumorigenesis in the cerebellum, beginning with ectopic proliferation of granule neuron progenitor cells.
source: Ptch+/− mice progress through well-defined stages of tumorigenesis in the cerebellum, beginning with the ectopic proliferation of granule neuron progenitor cells (GNPs), which form preneoplastic lesions on the cerebellar surface by two weeks of age.
evidence: This describes the established progression model in Ptch+/− mice, representing knowledge from the literature.

claim: Most preneoplastic lesions in Ptch+/− mice regress, while a minority undergo malignant transformation to medulloblastoma.
source: While most of these lesions regress, a minority undergo malignant transformation to MB (Kessler et al., 2009; Oliver et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Kessler et al., 2009; Oliver et al., 2005).

claim: Norrin/Frizzled4 pathway regulates vascular development in the cerebellum via neural/endothelial interactions.
source: Here, we modelled pre-tumor/stromal crosstalk during Ptch+/− MB evolution by manipulating the Norrin/Frizzled4 (Fzd4) pathway, an endogenous signalling axis that regulates vascular development in the cerebellum via neural/endothelial interactions (Wang et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2004; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Wang et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2004; Zhou et al., 2014).

claim: 24% of Ptch+/− lesions at P14 show vascular invasion.
source: To assess the stromal compartment at early stages of tumorigenesis in the Ptch+/− cerebellum, we sampled entire lesions at postnatal day (P) 14 by Collagen IV+ immunostaining, and observed an invasion of vasculature in a minority (24%; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Vascularized Ptch+/− lesions at P14 are statistically larger than non-vascularized lesions.
source: Furthermore, lesion volume, which is a measure of neoplastic progression in the Ptch+/− model, was statistically larger in vascularized lesions (mean 0.18 mm3) compared to non-vascularized ones (mean 0.029 mm3, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from lesion volume measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Norrin is a secreted atypical Wnt ligand that signals specifically through the Fzd4 receptor.
source: Norrin (encoded by the X-linked gene Ndp) is a secreted atypical Wnt ligand that signals specifically through the Fzd4 receptor and the Lrp5/6 and Tspan12 co-receptors to activate the canonical Wnt pathway in endothelial cells (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is established knowledge about Norrin signaling, illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Norrin is required for blood brain barrier integrity in the cerebellum.
source: Norrin (encoded by the X-linked gene Ndp) is a secreted atypical Wnt ligand that signals specifically through the Fzd4 receptor and the Lrp5/6 and Tspan12 co-receptors to activate the canonical Wnt pathway in endothelial cells (Figure 1C), where it is required for blood brain barrier (BBB) integrity in the cerebellum (Junge et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Junge et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2004).

claim: Ndp is expressed in the Purkinje cell layer of the cerebellum.
source: Consistent with alkaline phosphatase-based reporter data (Ye et al., 2010a), we detected Ndp expression in the Purkinje cell layer, presumably in Bergmann glia (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on X-gal staining data shown in Figure 1D and consistent with cited literature (Ye et al., 2010a).

claim: Ndp is expressed in the cerebellar external granule layer where granule neuron progenitors reside.
source: We also detected Ndp expression in the cerebellar external granule layer (EGL), where GNPs, the Shh-MB cell of origin, reside throughout postnatal development (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on X-gal staining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ndp expression is concentrated in the outer, proliferative region of the external granule layer at P7.
source: Combined X-gal staining and immunohistochemistry (IHC) during the peak period of GNP proliferation at P7 revealed that Ndp expression is concentrated in the outer region of the Pax6+ EGL, in the proliferative phospho-histone H3 (PH3)+ compartment (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on combined X-gal staining and immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ndp-expressing cells overlap with myelin basic protein-positive white matter, implicating oligodendrocytes as a source of Norrin.
source: β-gal+ cells also overlapped with myelin basic protein (MBP)+ white matter (Figure 1D) implicating oligodendrocytes as another source of Norrin.
evidence: This is based on co-staining data shown in Figure 1D, with inference about cell type identity.

claim: Ndp expression exhibits a downward trend in Ptch+/− GNPs at the lesion progression stage (P30) that reaches significance by the tumor stage.
source: While Ndp levels in Ptch+/− GNPs from pre-lesion (P7) and early lesion (P14) stages were comparable, Ndp expression exhibited a downward trend in GNPs at a lesion progression stage (P30) that reached significance by the tumor stage (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: NDP expression is enriched in human Shh-subgroup medulloblastoma compared to other molecular subgroups.
source: In human MB, NDP expression is enriched specifically in the Shh subgroup compared to the other three molecularly distinct subgroups: Wnt, driven by aberrant Wnt pathway activation, and Group 3 and 4, which are less clearly defined biologically (Taylor et al., 2012) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is based on expression profiling data from human MB samples shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There is a trend towards reduced survival in Shh-MB patients with tumors exhibiting the lowest levels of NDP expression.
source: Based on a limited sample size, we observed a trend towards reduced survival in Shh-MB patients with tumors exhibiting the lowest levels of NDP expression compared to those with the highest (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is based on survival analysis shown in Figure 1G, though the authors note the sample size is limited.

claim: Germ-line deletion of Ndp does not result in tumors in mice.
source: While germ-line deletion of the ligand Ndp (NdpKO) or conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells via the Tie2Cre driver (Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl) alone did not result in tumors
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells does not result in tumors in mice.
source: While germ-line deletion of the ligand Ndp (NdpKO) or conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells via the Tie2Cre driver (Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl) alone did not result in tumors
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Deletion of Ndp dramatically accelerates medulloblastoma formation in Ptch+/− mice.
source: While germ-line deletion of the ligand Ndp (NdpKO) or conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells via the Tie2Cre driver (Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl) alone did not result in tumors, both mutations dramatically accelerated MB formation and significantly reduced survival in Ptch+/− mice (Figure 2A–C)
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figures 2A-C.

claim: Conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells dramatically accelerates medulloblastoma formation in Ptch+/− mice.
source: While germ-line deletion of the ligand Ndp (NdpKO) or conditional deletion of Fzd4 in endothelial cells via the Tie2Cre driver (Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl) alone did not result in tumors, both mutations dramatically accelerated MB formation and significantly reduced survival in Ptch+/− mice (Figure 2A–C)
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figures 2A-C.

claim: In NdpKO;Ptch+/− mice, MB incidence increased by approximately two-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates.
source: In both NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/−compound mutants, MB incidence increased by approximately two-fold and mean latency was reduced more than two-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from survival studies summarized in Figure 2C.

claim: In NdpKO;Ptch+/− mice, mean MB latency was reduced more than two-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates.
source: In both NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/−compound mutants, MB incidence increased by approximately two-fold and mean latency was reduced more than two-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from survival studies summarized in Figure 2C.

claim: Endogenous FZD4 protein is expressed in isolated GNPs.
source: In isolated GNPs, we detected the expression of endogenous FZD4 protein (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Transcripts of Fzd4, Lrp5 and Tspan12 are expressed in isolated GNPs.
source: In isolated GNPs, we detected the expression of endogenous FZD4 protein (Figure 2D), and transcripts of Fzd4, Lrp5 and Tspan12 (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Conditional deletion of Fzd4 from GNPs in the Ptch+/− model has no impact on survival and tumorigenesis.
source: however, conditional deletion of Fzd4 from GNPs in the Ptch+/− model had no impact on survival and tumorigenesis (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The tumor inhibitory role of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling in Ptch+/− MB is mediated by the endothelial cell component of the tumor stroma.
source: These results reveal a novel tumor inhibitory role for Norrin/Fzd4 signalling in Ptch+/−MB that, strikingly, is mediated by the endothelial cell component of the tumor stroma.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of endothelial-specific versus GNP-specific Fzd4 deletion shown in Figures 2B and 2F.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− medulloblastomas exhibit classic histology.
source: To gain insight into Norrin-mediated effects on Ptch+/− tumorigenesis, we examined established NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− MBs by histology and expression profiling. Both tumor types exhibited classic histology
evidence: This is based on H&E staining shown in Figure 3A.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− medulloblastomas exhibit similar expression patterns for Shh-MB neural markers (Atoh1, TUBB3 and GFAP).
source: Both tumor types exhibited classic histology, and similar expression patterns for expected Shh-MB neural markers (Atoh1, TUBB3 and GFAP) and Hh target genes (Gli1, Mycn and Ccnd1) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization and immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− medulloblastomas exhibit similar expression patterns for Hh target genes (Gli1, Mycn and Ccnd1).
source: Both tumor types exhibited classic histology, and similar expression patterns for expected Shh-MB neural markers (Atoh1, TUBB3 and GFAP) and Hh target genes (Gli1, Mycn and Ccnd1) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Both NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− tumors contain a stromal component revealed by laminin and CD31 immunostaining.
source: Co-immunostaining for the ECM protein laminin and the vascular endothelial cell marker CD31 (PECAM1; platelet/endothelial cell adhesion molecule 1) revealed a stromal component in both tumors (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− tumors have clearly separable gene expression signatures.
source: However, tumor heterogeneity poses challenges to histological-based classification, therefore we turned to whole genome expression profiling, where hierarchical clustering and principal component analysis revealed that NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− tumors have clearly separable gene expression signatures (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on whole genome expression profiling data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors are enriched for changes in stromal genes compared to Ptch+/− tumors, particularly ECM components.
source: Consistent with a stromal requirement for Norrin/Fzd4 signalling, tumors in NdpKO;Ptch+/− mutants were enriched for changes in stromal genes compared to their Ptch+/− counterparts, particularly ECM components (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: Esm1, Plvap and Emcn are up-regulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors compared to Ptch+/− tumors.
source: Up-regulated genes in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors included components of endothelial cells, including Esm1 (Endothelial cell-specific molecule 1), Plvap (Plasmalemmal vesicle associated protein) and Emcn (Endomucin) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D), which we validated by qRT-PCR (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on microarray and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Up-regulation of Plvap in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors is associated with increased vascular permeability demonstrated by enhanced Evans blue leakage.
source: The up-regulation of Plvap, a marker of fenestrated endothelial cells, was associated with increased vascular permeability in NdpKO;Ptch+/− versus Ptch+/− tumors, demonstrated by enhanced leakage of the serum protein binding dye Evans blue (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is based on Evans blue leakage assay shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Pecam1 is upregulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors compared to Ptch+/− tumors, suggesting increased vascularity.
source: Additional genes upregulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− versus Ptch+/− tumors by qRT-PCR were Pecam1, suggesting increased vascularity in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F, with inference about biological significance.

claim: Angpt2 is upregulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors compared to Ptch+/− tumors.
source: Additional genes upregulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− versus Ptch+/− tumors by qRT-PCR were Pecam1, suggesting increased vascularity in NdpKO;Ptch+/− tumors, and the angiogenic regulator Angpt2 (Angiopoietin-2) (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Loss of Norrin modulates features of the tumor stroma rather than impacting Shh signalling.
source: These results suggest that rather than impacting Shh signalling, loss of Norrin modulates features of the tumor stroma.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar expression of Hh target genes but differential stromal gene expression between NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Ptch+/− tumors.

claim: The number of cerebellar lesions in NdpKO;Ptch+/− mutants at P14 is increased 3.9-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates.
source: At P14, the earliest stage when lesions are consistently detected in Ptch+/− mice, the number of cerebellar lesions in NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− mutants was increased 3.9-fold and 2.4-fold, respectively, compared their Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from lesion counting shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The number of cerebellar lesions in Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− mutants at P14 is increased 2.4-fold compared to Ptch+/− littermates.
source: At P14, the earliest stage when lesions are consistently detected in Ptch+/− mice, the number of cerebellar lesions in NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− mutants was increased 3.9-fold and 2.4-fold, respectively, compared their Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from lesion counting shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The effect of Norrin/Fzd4 loss on lesion number at P14 is not associated with changes to the Ptch+/− cerebellum at prior ages.
source: This effect on lesion number was not associated with changes to the Ptch+/− cerebellum at prior ages, as we failed to detect separable GNP expression profiles or general overgrowth of the EGL in NdpKO;Ptch+/− versus Ptch+/− cerebella at P6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on expression profiling and EGL thickness measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of Ptch+/− lesions at P14 are poorly vascularized aside from existing meningeal blood vessels.
source: Consistent with our previous observations (Figure 1A), immunostaining for CD31 and laminin showed that the majority of Ptch+/− lesions were poorly vascularized, aside from existing blood vessels associated with the meninges at the cerebellar surface (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Compound mutant lesions (NdpKO;Ptch+/− and Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/−) exhibit irregular deposition of ECM.
source: In contrast, compound mutant lesions exhibited several hallmarks of angiogenic remodelling, including irregular deposition of ECM (Figure 5A)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining for laminin shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Compound mutant lesions exhibit an increased frequency of mitotic endothelial cells per vessel area.
source: In contrast, compound mutant lesions exhibited several hallmarks of angiogenic remodelling, including irregular deposition of ECM (Figure 5A), an increased frequency of mitotic endothelial cells per vessel area (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is based on quantification of PH3+CD31+ cells shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Compound mutant lesions exhibit an increase in vascular endothelial cell and laminin density.
source: In contrast, compound mutant lesions exhibited several hallmarks of angiogenic remodelling, including irregular deposition of ECM (Figure 5A), an increased frequency of mitotic endothelial cells per vessel area (Figure 5B), and an increase in vascular endothelial cell and laminin density (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on quantification of CD31 and laminin density shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Vascular remodelling in compound mutants is restricted to lesions, with only rare examples of disrupted morphology in the EGL.
source: This vascular remodelling was restricted to lesions, with only rare examples of disrupted morphology associated with the EGL in single Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl cerebella (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: 78% of NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions at P14 are vascularized compared to 24% of Ptch+/− lesions.
source: Interestingly, while the vast majority of compound mutant lesions were vascularized at P14 (78% NdpKO;Ptch+/− and 95% Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− versus 24% Ptch+/−;Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from lesion analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: 95% of Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− lesions at P14 are vascularized compared to 24% of Ptch+/− lesions.
source: Interestingly, while the vast majority of compound mutant lesions were vascularized at P14 (78% NdpKO;Ptch+/− and 95% Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− versus 24% Ptch+/−;Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from lesion analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Compound mutant lesion volume is not increased at P14 despite vascular remodelling.
source: Interestingly, while the vast majority of compound mutant lesions were vascularized at P14 (78% NdpKO;Ptch+/− and 95% Tie2Cre+;Fzd4fl/fl;Ptch+/− versus 24% Ptch+/−;Figure 5D), compound mutant lesion volume was not increased at this early stage of tumor evolution (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This is based on lesion volume measurements shown in Figures 4B and 4D.

claim: Vascular remodelling occurs in very small (<0.02 mm3) compound mutant lesions.
source: Accordingly, we observed vascular remodeling in very small (<0.02 mm3) compound mutant lesions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vascular remodelling induced by loss of Norrin/Fzd4 is independent of the increase in lesion volume.
source: Thus, vascular remodelling induced by loss of Norrin/Fzd4 is independent of the increase in lesion volume.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that vascular remodelling occurs in small lesions and before volume increases.

claim: Lesions in compound mutants show a marked loss of vascular integrity characterized by induction of PLVAP.
source: Consistent with the known role for Norrin/Fzd4 in normal BBB development and function [(Wang et al., 2012) and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B], lesions in compound mutants showed a marked loss of vascular integrity, characterized by induction of PLVAP (Figure 6A,B)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and quantification shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Lesions in compound mutants show variable loss of the tight junction protein Claudin-5.
source: Consistent with the known role for Norrin/Fzd4 in normal BBB development and function [(Wang et al., 2012) and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B], lesions in compound mutants showed a marked loss of vascular integrity, characterized by induction of PLVAP (Figure 6A,B), variable loss of the tight junction protein Claudin-5 (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Lesions in compound mutants show leakage of Evans blue.
source: Consistent with the known role for Norrin/Fzd4 in normal BBB development and function [(Wang et al., 2012) and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B], lesions in compound mutants showed a marked loss of vascular integrity, characterized by induction of PLVAP (Figure 6A,B), variable loss of the tight junction protein Claudin-5 (Figure 6A), and leakage of Evans blue (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on Evans blue leakage assay shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Single Ptch+/− mice never exhibit leaky vessels in lesions.
source: In contrast, single Ptch+/− mice never exhibited leaky vessels (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and Evans blue data shown in Figure 6A-C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Active Hh signalling positively regulates BBB maintenance.
source: In contrast, single Ptch+/− mice never exhibited leaky vessels (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B), which is consistent with the positive regulation of BBB maintenance by active Hh signalling (Alvarez et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Alvarez et al., 2011).

claim: The proportion of leaky lesions is significantly increased in compound mutants compared to Ptch+/−.
source: Accordingly, the proportion of leaky lesions was significantly increased in compound mutants compared to Ptch+/− (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding summarized in Figure 6D.

claim: Lesion-associated vessels in compound mutants do not show overt differences in pericyte coverage.
source: Lesion-associated vessels in compound mutants did not show overt differences in pericyte coverage (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E)
evidence: This is based on immunostaining for PDGFRβ shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Lesion-associated vessels in compound mutants exhibit a high frequency of perivascular accumulation of CD45+ leukocytes compared with Ptch+/− lesions.
source: however, they did exhibit a high frequency of perivascular accumulation of CD45+ leukocytes compared with Ptch+/− lesions (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and quantification shown in Figures 6D and 6E.

claim: Loss of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling to endothelial cells accelerates the transition to a tumor-permissive stroma characterized by vascular permeability, inflammation and angiogenic remodelling.
source: Together, these results show that loss of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling to endothelial cells accelerates the transition to a tumor-permissive stroma characterized by vascular permeability, inflammation and angiogenic remodelling.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the collective data from Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The angiogenic switch promotes preneoplastic progression of non-CNS tumors.
source: These changes are reminiscent of the switch to angiogenesis that promotes the preneoplastic progression of non-central nervous system (CNS) tumors (Baeriswyl and Christofori, 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Baeriswyl and Christofori, 2009).

claim: Angpt2 is involved in the angiogenic switch in non-CNS tumors.
source: These changes are reminiscent of the switch to angiogenesis that promotes the preneoplastic progression of non-central nervous system (CNS) tumors (Baeriswyl and Christofori, 2009), where the range of cellular and molecular players involved include Angpt2 (Mazzieri et al., 2011; Rigamonti et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Mazzieri et al., 2011; Rigamonti et al., 2014).

claim: Endothelial Lef1 expression in P14 NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions is significantly reduced compared to P14 Ptch+/− lesions and EGL.
source: Endothelial Lef1 expression in P14 NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions was significantly reduced compared to P14 Ptch+/− lesions and EGL (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B), confirming the Ndp dependence of this marker in the endothelium.
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Endothelial Lef1 expression in vascularized Ptch+/− lesions is downregulated compared to adjacent EGL.
source: While Lef1 expression in the endothelium of non-vascularized Ptch+/− lesions was similar to that in adjacent EGL, we observed a downregulation of endothelial Lef1 expression in vascularized Ptch+/− lesions compared to EGL (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is based on quantification shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Lesion progression in Ptch+/− mice may be associated with a reduction in endogenous canonical Wnt activity in the endothelium.
source: These data suggest that lesion progression in Ptch+/− mice may be associated with a reduction in endogenous canonical Wnt activity in the endothelium
evidence: This is inferred from the Lef1 expression data and the downward trend in Ndp expression during lesion progression.

claim: αFzd4 treatment of Ptch+/− mice at P7 and P16 increases MB incidence from 69% to 93%.
source: αFzd4 treatment of Ptch+/−mice at P7 and P16 was sufficient to phenocopy the enhanced tumor initiation phenotype of our compound mutant models, increasing MB incidence from 69% in animals injected with anti-keyhole limpet hemocyanin (αKLH) control antibody to 93% in those injected with αFzd4
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the survival study shown in Figure 7A.

claim: αFzd4 treatment of Ptch+/− mice at P7 and P16 significantly reduces mean tumor latency from 167 to 104 days.
source: αFzd4 treatment of Ptch+/−mice at P7 and P16 was sufficient to phenocopy the enhanced tumor initiation phenotype of our compound mutant models, increasing MB incidence from 69% in animals injected with anti-keyhole limpet hemocyanin (αKLH) control antibody to 93% in those injected with αFzd4, and significantly reducing mean tumor latency from 167 to 104 days (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the survival study shown in Figure 7A.

claim: A single dose of αFzd4 administered at P7 is sufficient to increase the number of lesions at P14.
source: Furthermore, a single dose of αFzd4 administered as late as P7 was sufficient to increase number (but not volume) of lesions at P14 (Figure 7B)
evidence: This is based on lesion quantification shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A single dose of αFzd4 administered at P7 does not increase lesion volume at P14.
source: Furthermore, a single dose of αFzd4 administered as late as P7 was sufficient to increase number (but not volume) of lesions at P14 (Figure 7B)
evidence: This is based on lesion volume measurements shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A single dose of αFzd4 administered at P7 converts lesions to a leaky vasculature phenotype.
source: Furthermore, a single dose of αFzd4 administered as late as P7 was sufficient to increase number (but not volume) of lesions at P14 (Figure 7B), convert lesions to a leaky vasculature phenotype (Figure 7C,I)
evidence: This is based on Evans blue leakage data shown in Figures 7C and 7I.

claim: A single dose of αFzd4 administered at P7 significantly increases the proportion of vascularized lesions compared to αKLH controls.
source: Furthermore, a single dose of αFzd4 administered as late as P7 was sufficient to increase number (but not volume) of lesions at P14 (Figure 7B), convert lesions to a leaky vasculature phenotype (Figure 7C,I), and significantly increase the proportion of vascularized lesions compared to αKLH controls (Figure 7D,I).
evidence: This is based on lesion vascularization analysis shown in Figures 7D and 7I.

claim: Acute disruption of Fzd4 promotes the conversion to an angiogenic, pro-tumor stroma within seven days.
source: Thus, acute disruption of Fzd4 promotes the conversion to an angiogenic, pro-tumor stroma within seven days, suggesting that continued maintenance of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling creates a tumor-protective microenvironment.
evidence: This is inferred from the rapid effects of αFzd4 treatment observed within 7 days (P7 to P14).

claim: Ptx treatment compromises paracellular permeability in the P14 cerebellum by disrupting endothelial cell tight junctions.
source: Ptx treatment compromised paracellular permeability in the P14 cerebellum by disrupting endothelial cell tight junctions via reduced ZO-1 and Claudin-5 expression, accompanied by Evans Blue leakage (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B and data not shown).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Ptx-mediated BBB disruption is independent of PLVAP induction.
source: This Ptx-mediated effect on BBB integrity was independent of PLVAP induction (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C), an indicator of transcellular openings (Stan et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Ptx treatment of Ptch+/− mice does not affect MB incidence or latency compared to PBS-injected controls.
source: Ptx treatment of Ptch+/− mice did not affect MB incidence or latency compared to Ptch+/− PBS-injected controls (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Despite vascular permeability in lesions of Ptx-treated Ptch+/− mice, the number, volume and proportion of vascularized lesions are not changed.
source: Furthermore, despite vascular permeability as seen by Evans Blue leakage in lesions of Ptx-treated Ptch+/− mice, the number, volume and proportion of vascularized lesions were not changed (Figure 7F–I).
evidence: This is based on lesion analysis shown in Figures 7F-I.

claim: Ptx-induced BBB disruption alone does not drive lesion formation, lesion angiogenesis, or tumor initiation.
source: These data show that Ptx-induced BBB disruption alone does not drive lesion formation, lesion angiogenesis, or tumor initiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effects of Ptx treatment on lesion parameters and tumor outcomes.

claim: P14 lesions of NdpKO;Ptch+/− mutants show a modest but significant increase in mitotic index compared to Ptch+/− lesions.
source: We first observed a modest, but significant, increase in the mitotic index of P14 lesions of NdpKO;Ptch+/− mutants compared to their Ptch+/− counterparts (Figure 8A)
evidence: This is based on PH3 immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 8A.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions exhibit less Cleaved Caspase 3 immunostaining compared to Ptch+/− lesions.
source: which was not counterbalanced by enhanced cell death or differentiation, as NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions exhibited less Cleaved Caspase 3 immunostaining and comparable expression levels of the differentiation marker NeuN compared to their Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 8A.

claim: NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions show comparable expression levels of the differentiation marker NeuN compared to Ptch+/− lesions.
source: which was not counterbalanced by enhanced cell death or differentiation, as NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions exhibited less Cleaved Caspase 3 immunostaining and comparable expression levels of the differentiation marker NeuN compared to their Ptch+/− littermates (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The increased mitotic index in NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions at P14 does not translate into increased lesion volume at this stage.
source: Interestingly, this increased mitotic index did not translate into increased lesion volume at this stage (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This is based on lesion volume measurements shown in Figures 4B and 4D.

claim: Pax6+EdU+ S-phase GNPs are present in the vicinity of blood vessels in Ptch+/− and NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions.
source: We examined the relationship between proliferating GNPs and lesion vasculature by Pax6/CD31/EdU triple staining, and found that Pax6+EdU+ S-phase GNPs were present in the vicinity of blood vessels in Ptch+/− or NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on triple immunostaining shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Enhanced proliferation and DNA damage in pre-malignant GNPs leads to increased incidence and decreased latency of MB in the Ptch+/− model.
source: In the Ptch+/− MB context, enhanced proliferation and DNA damage in pre-malignant GNPs leads to increased incidence and decreased latency of MB (Ayrault et al., 2009; Leonard et al., 2008; Mille et al., 2014; Uziel et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Ayrault et al., 2009; Leonard et al., 2008; Mille et al., 2014; Uziel et al., 2005).

claim: Ptch loss of heterozygosity is a well-established indicator of malignant progression in the Ptch+/− model.
source: Here, Ptch loss of heterozygosity (LOH; where the remaining wild-type Ptch allele is inactivated) is a well-established indicator of malignant progression in this model (Mille et al., 2014; Pazzaglia et al., 2006a; 2006b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Mille et al., 2014; Pazzaglia et al., 2006a; 2006b).

claim: At P14, the frequency of Ptch LOH is increased in NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions (9/17) compared to Ptch+/− lesions (3/14).
source: At this stage, the frequency of Ptch LOH was increased in NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions (9/17) compared to Ptch+/− lesions (3/14).
evidence: This is based on Ptch LOH analysis by qRT-PCR of microdissected lesions shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The shorter MB latency observed upon Ndp loss-of-function is characterized by an accelerated rate of Ptch LOH.
source: Thus, the shorter MB latency observed upon Ndp loss-of-function is characterized by an accelerated rate of Ptch LOH.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased frequency of Ptch LOH in NdpKO;Ptch+/− lesions at P14.

claim: Deletion of Ndp dramatically accelerates cerebellar tumorigenesis in Neurod2-SmoA1+/− mice, reducing mean latency from 167 to 34 days.
source: Deletion of Ndp dramatically accelerated cerebellar tumorigenesis in Neurod2-SmoA1+/− mice, reducing mean latency almost 5-fold, from 167 to 34 days (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is based on Kaplan-Meier survival data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The tumor inhibitory effects of Norrin signaling extend to oncogene-driven Shh MB.
source: Thus, the tumor inhibitory effects of Norrin signaling extend to oncogene-driven Shh MB.
evidence: This is inferred from the effects of Ndp deletion in the Neurod2-SmoA1 model shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The tumor microenvironment is a critical modulator of carcinogenesis.
source: The tumor microenvironment is a critical modulator of carcinogenesis; however, in many tumor types, the influence of the stroma during preneoplastic stages is unknown.
evidence: This is general knowledge in the field of cancer biology.

claim: Construction of a tumor-permissive stroma is a dynamic process influencing all stages of malignant progression.
source: It has also become increasingly clear that construction of a tumor-permissive stroma is a dynamic process influencing all stages of malignant progression, through the ongoing extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and recruitment or activation of angiogenic vascular cells, fibroblasts and immune cells (Hanahan and Coussens, 2012; Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Hanahan and Coussens, 2012; Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).

claim: A permissive niche is required during the earliest steps of tumor initiation.
source: While there is mounting evidence that a permissive niche is required during the earliest steps of tumor initiation, studying this early crosstalk requires adequate multistage models of carcinogenesis (Barcellos-Hoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Barcellos-Hoff et al., 2013).

claim: Little is known about tumor/stromal communication in the early stages of medulloblastoma.
source: Medulloblastoma (MB), the most common malignant brain tumor in children, has become a paradigm for the study of pediatric tumors and primary brain tumors; however little is known about tumor/stromal communication in the early stages of MB.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: MB cell lines frequently fail to maintain their in vivo characteristics.
source: It is challenging to model these early events with human tumor biopsies or MB cell lines, as both represent late stage tumors and the latter frequently fail to maintain their in vivo characteristics (Sasai et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Sasai et al., 2006).

claim: The Ptch+/− mouse is a model of human Gorlin syndrome that belongs to the Sonic hedgehog subgroup of medulloblastoma.
source: An effective surrogate to test these interactions endogenously is the Ptch+/− mouse (Goodrich et al., 1997), a model of the human predisposition to MB (Gorlin syndrome) that, along with a subset of sporadic MB, belong to the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) subgroup (Taylor et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Goodrich et al., 1997; Taylor et al., 2012).

claim: The environmental signals that co-operate with Ptch haploinsufficiency to regulate lesion induction and transformation are poorly understood.
source: The environmental signals that co-operate with Ptch haploinsufficiency to regulate lesion induction and transformation are poorly understood.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: This is the first study to describe a stromal component to the early stages of Shh-driven tumor initiation in the brain.
source: This is the first study to describe a stromal component to the early stages of Shh-driven tumor initiation in the brain.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study's findings.

claim: Activation of angiogenesis and stromal remodelling are key features of the oncogenic microenvironment that dramatically accelerates tumorigenesis in the Ptch+/− cerebellum.
source: We show that activation of angiogenesis and stromal remodelling are key features of the oncogenic microenvironment that dramatically accelerates tumorigenesis in the Ptch+/ cerebellum.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings based on data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Mutations in Norrin/Fzd4 pathway components cause a spectrum of human pathologies, including vascular disorders with retinal and cerebellar phenotypes.
source: Mutations in Norrin/Fzd4 pathway components cause a spectrum of human pathologies, including vascular disorders with retinal and cerebellar phenotypes (Gilmour, 2015; Liu et al., 2010; Romaniello et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gilmour, 2015; Liu et al., 2010; Romaniello et al., 2013).

claim: The role of the Norrin/Fzd4 signalling axis in the vasculature has not been explored in human tumorigenesis.
source: However, the role of this signalling axis in the vasculature has not been explored in human tumorigenesis.
evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge.

claim: NDP mRNA levels are generally high in human Shh-MB.
source: While we did observe a trend towards reduced survival in Shh-MB patients with the lowest levels of NDP transcript, NDP mRNA levels are generally high in human Shh-MB, suggesting a potential protective role for this pathway.
evidence: This is based on expression profiling data from human MB samples shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The activities of several angiogenic factors, including VEGF and FGF, are regulated at the level of protein bioavailability.
source: Notably, the activities of several angiogenic factors, including VEGF and FGF, are regulated at the level of protein bioavailability (Hynes, 2009), requiring release from the ECM to mediate angiogenesis in pre-tumor lesions (Bergers et al., 2000; Nozawa et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Hynes, 2009; Bergers et al., 2000; Nozawa et al., 2006).

claim: Norrin associates with the ECM.
source: Interestingly, Norrin also associates with the ECM (Perez-Vilar and Hill, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Perez-Vilar and Hill, 1997).

claim: Wnt-mediated neural/endothelial crosstalk plays a role in CNS vascular development and pathology.
source: Nonetheless, given the known role of Wnt-mediated neural/endothelial crosstalk in CNS vascular development and pathology (Engelhardt and Liebner, 2014; Phoenix et al., 2016; Ye et al., 2010b), our work highlights the importance of further examining the Norrin/Fzd4 pathway in the human MB progression, including a potential prophylactic role in susceptible individuals.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Engelhardt and Liebner, 2014; Phoenix et al., 2016; Ye et al., 2010b).

claim: Ptch+/− lesion induction is mediated by growth or differentiation regulators including Igf1, Ccnd1, and Tis21.
source: Ptch+/− lesion induction is known to be mediated by growth or differentiation regulators [Igf1, Ccnd1, Tis21 (Farioli-Vecchioli et al., 2012; Pogoriler et al., 2006; Tanori et al., 2010)]
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Farioli-Vecchioli et al., 2012; Pogoriler et al., 2006; Tanori et al., 2010).

claim: Ptch+/− lesion induction is mediated by radiation or interference with DNA repair.
source: Ptch+/− lesion induction is known to be mediated by growth or differentiation regulators [Igf1, Ccnd1, Tis21 (Farioli-Vecchioli et al., 2012; Pogoriler et al., 2006; Tanori et al., 2010)] and by radiation or interference with DNA repair (Malek et al., 2011; Pazzaglia et al., 2006a; 2006b)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Malek et al., 2011; Pazzaglia et al., 2006a; 2006b).

claim: Progression of Ptch+/− lesions to malignancy is enhanced by Igf2, Mycn, Shh co-receptor Boc and by evasion of p53-induced senescence.
source: whereas progression of lesions to malignancy is enhanced by the growth promoting factors Igf2, Mycn, Shh co-receptor Boc and by the evasion of p53-induced senescence (Corcoran et al., 2008; Kessler et al., 2009; Mille et al., 2014; Tamayo-Orrego et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Corcoran et al., 2008; Kessler et al., 2009; Mille et al., 2014; Tamayo-Orrego et al., 2016).

claim: The pro-tumor stroma induced by loss of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling is linked to increased GNP proliferation and accelerated Ptch LOH.
source: We have linked the pro-tumor stroma induced by loss of Norrin/Fzd4 signalling to increased GNP proliferation and accelerated Ptch LOH, both events that are known to increase the incidence and decrease latency of Ptch+/− MB (Ayrault et al., 2009; Mille et al., 2014; Pazzaglia et al., 2006a; 2006b; Uziel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 8 and supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Development of an oncogenic niche supports the growth and transformation of preneoplastic cells.
source: These data add to accumulating evidence that development of an oncogenic niche supports the growth and transformation of preneoplastic cells (Barcellos-Hoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Barcellos-Hoff et al., 2013).

claim: Modulation of Wnt-mediated BBB characteristics in orthotopic transplants of established mouse MB does not impact tumor incidence or survival.
source: Similarly, a recent study showed that modulation of Wnt-mediated BBB characteristics in orthotopic transplants of established mouse MB did not impact the tumor incidence or survival (Phoenix et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Phoenix et al., 2016).

claim: Ptch+/− vascular endothelial cells may exhibit elevated Hh pathway activity.
source: We recognize that Ptch+/− vascular endothelial cells in the germ-line Ptch+/− model may exhibit elevated Hh pathway activity
evidence: This is speculation based on the genetic model.

claim: Norrin-dependent effects on tumorigenesis are independent of Ptch status in the endothelium.
source: Furthermore, our data showing dramatic acceleration of tumor formation upon deletion of Ndp from the Neurod2-SmoA1 MB model demonstrate that Norrin-dependent effects on tumorigenesis are independent of Ptch status in the endothelium.
evidence: This is inferred from the effects in the Neurod2-SmoA1 model shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Attenuation of Wnt signaling in endothelial cells and vascular invasion are endogenous factors regulating Ptch+/− lesion progression.
source: Our work suggests that attenuation of Wnt signaling in endothelial cells and vascular invasion are endogenous factors regulating Ptch+/− lesion progression.
evidence: This is inferred from the collective data on Lef1 expression and vascular changes in lesions.

claim: Fzd4-deficient endothelial cells exhibit transcript enrichment for genes known to promote GNP growth (Igf1) and angiogenesis (Angpt2 and Esm1).
source: Interestingly, previous work analyzing the transcriptomes of Fzd4KO versus Fzd4 WT endothelial cells isolated from the adult mouse retina and P16 cerebellum (Ye et al., 2009) showed that Fzd4-deficient endothelial cells exhibit transcript enrichment for genes known to promote both GNP growth (Igf1) and angiogenesis (Angpt2 and Esm1, both of which were upregulated in NdpKO;Ptch+/− versus Ptch+/− MB).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Ye et al., 2009) and data from the current study.

claim: The Tie2Cre driver is expressed in hematopoietic lineages.
source: The Tie2Cre driver used to delete Fzd4 is also expressed in hematopoietic lineages (Tang et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Tang et al., 2010).

claim: In pancreatic and breast cancer models, the angiogenic switch occurs prior to malignancy and may be a rate limiting step for tumor initiation.
source: Mouse models of these tumors have shown that the angiogenic switch, in particular, occurs prior to malignancy and may be a rate limiting step for tumor initiation (Giraudo et al., 2004; Hanahan et al., 1996; Lin et al., 2006; Smith-McCune et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Giraudo et al., 2004; Hanahan et al., 1996; Lin et al., 2006; Smith-McCune et al., 1997).

claim: In pancreatic and breast tumor models, the angiogenic switch is not correlated with size in early-stage lesions, but is associated with the transition from preneoplasia to malignancy.
source: These data reflect previous studies in pancreatic and breast tumor models, where the angiogenic switch was not correlated with size in early-stage lesions, but was instead associated with, and required for, the transition from preneoplasia to malignancy (Folkman et al., 1989; Lin et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Folkman et al., 1989; Lin et al., 2006).
